summary: Hospitality operations: guest requests routed to housekeeping, maintenance, kitchen and front desk, with rooms, staff on duty and who is handling what.

actions.name: list_requests
actions.title: List guest requests
actions.description: Lists guest requests, newest first: request, room, department (housekeeping, maintenance, food, front_desk), priority (low, normal, high, urgent), status (new, assigned, in_progress, done, cancelled; empty means new), who it is assigned to, guest and note. Filter by status, department or room.

actions.name: get_request
actions.title: Read a guest request
actions.description: Reads one guest request by its row id: request, room, department, priority, status, assignee, guest and note.

actions.name: create_request
actions.title: Log a guest request
actions.description: Logs a new guest request for a room, e.g. room 204: two extra towels. department is housekeeping, maintenance, food or front_desk; priority is low, normal, high or urgent (urgent only for safety or a room the guest cannot use). Leave status empty: a new request is new.

actions.name: update_request
actions.title: Update a guest request
actions.description: Changes a guest request by row id. To assign: status assigned, assignee a name exactly as list_staff gives it, and assignee_email that person's email. Other statuses: in_progress, done, cancelled. Can also change priority or add a note.

actions.name: list_rooms
actions.title: List rooms
actions.description: Lists rooms with floor, status (available, occupied, cleaning, maintenance) and guest. Filter by status, e.g. cleaning for rooms not ready yet.

actions.name: update_room
actions.title: Change a room
actions.description: Changes a room by its number or row id: status (available, occupied, cleaning, maintenance) or guest. maintenance takes it out of service.

actions.name: list_staff
actions.title: List staff
actions.description: Lists staff with email, department (housekeeping, maintenance, food, front_desk) and whether they are on duty. Filter by department or on_duty to see who can take work now.

skills.name: shift-handover
skills.title: Shift handover
skills.instructions:
Shift handover for NEXORA.

Use this at shift change or when someone asks for a handover, a shift report or what is still open.

1. Gather facts with the read tools only: list_requests (status new, then assigned, then in_progress), list_staff with on_duty true, and list_rooms with status cleaning and then maintenance. Use only what they return; never invent requests, rooms or names. Name a request by room and request, e.g. Room 311 - AC not cooling.

2. Write the handover, short and scannable:
- Headline: totals of new, assigned and in progress.
- Unassigned (status new or empty): room, request, department, priority. Urgent and high first.
- In hand: room, request, who has it.
- Rooms not ready: cleaning or out of service.
Leave out empty sections.

3. Propose an owner for each unassigned request: someone on duty in the matching department, preferring whoever has the fewest requests already. If nobody suitable is on duty, say so and suggest the duty manager. Show proposals as a numbered list.

4. Act only after the person confirms which to apply. For each, call update_request with status assigned, assignee the name exactly as list_staff gave it, and assignee_email that person's email. Report each result; one failure does not stop the rest.

Be brief and factual: tired staff read this at shift change.
